songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Rare early‑70 set with debut “Friend of the Devil” and blazing Viola Lee Blues
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a high‑energy early‑1970 performance featuring the debut of “Friend of the Devil,” a scorching “Viola Lee Blues” → “The Seven” jam, and solid folk‑rock cuts like “Me & My Uncle.” Jerry’s guitar swings from raw psychedelia to tight rhythm, while Phil adds an adventurous Cumberland Blues improvisation. The recommended audience recording captures the excitement with excellent fidelity.
ai_show_review.review:
Port Chester’s March 21, 1970 early show is a historic snapshot of the Dead as they transitioned from folk‑rock newcomers into a tighter jam band. Highlights include the first known performance of “Friend of the Devil,” a fierce “Viola Lee Blues” that morphs into an expansive “The Seven” and a spontaneous Cumberland Blues jam, plus strong renditions of “Me & My Uncle,” “Dire Wolf,” and “Death Don't Have No Mercy.” Jerry’s playing is at times “all over the place,” yet his deep, primal blues tone on Viola Lee shines, while Phil’s bass work ignites the improvisational spark during The Seven. Although the set has a few uneven moments—“Walkin’ The Dog” was noted as sloppy—the overall energy and rarity of material make it a must‑listen for completists.

Two audience recordings exist; the second (gd70-03-21.early.lee.pcrp.20184.sbeok.shnf) is widely praised as the “best AUD source from 1970,” delivering crystal‑clear sound that preserves both the band’s dynamics and the crowd’s enthusiasm, making it the optimal listening choice.

best_recording.reason: Excellent audience tape with crystal‑clear sound, captures the high‑energy performance and crowd ambience; praised as the best 1970 AUD source.
